definitions.gloss: auspicious; lucky; of good omen; bringing good fortune
definitions.explanation: Describing something that is considered a sign of good luck or that brings favorable outcomes. Deeply rooted in Japanese folk beliefs about omens and fortune.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}は{縁起|えんぎ}が{良|い}い{色|いろ}だ。
{鶴|つる}と{亀|かめ}は{縁起|えんぎ}が{良|い}いとされている。
examples.english: Cranes and turtles are considered to bring good luck.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}に{縁起|えんぎ}の{良|い}い{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{食|た}べるのが{日本|にほん}の{習慣|しゅうかん}だ。
examples.english: It is a Japanese custom to eat auspicious foods at New Year.

notes:
USAGE:
{縁起|えんぎ} refers to omens or signs of fortune, and {縁起|えんぎ}が{良|い}い means something is a good omen. Often used in the context of traditional Japanese customs, especially around New Year, weddings, and other celebrations. The opposite is {縁起|えんぎ}が{悪|わる}い (unlucky, of bad omen).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {縁起|えんぎ}の{良|い}い{数字|すうじ} (lucky number)
- {縁起|えんぎ}の{良|い}い{食|た}べ{物|もの} (auspicious food)
- {縁起|えんぎ}を{担|かつ}ぐ (to be superstitious about omens)
- {縁起物|えんぎもの} (lucky charm)

CONTRAST:
- {縁起|えんぎ}が{悪|わる}い: unlucky, of bad omen — the direct opposite
- {幸運|こううん}: good fortune — more about actual luck than omens
- {吉|きち}: good luck, auspiciousness — used in fortune-telling contexts
